context.analysis:
## Overview
[The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud before approval and provides case management for suspicious transactions. Its core purpose is to deliver sub-50ms fraud decisions at 3,000 TPS while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability.]

## Key Elements
* Payment Gateway / Acquirer
* Cardholder / Customer
* Fraud Analyst & Risk Manager
* Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System
* Payment Network / Card Brands (Visa/Mastercard)
* Core Ledger / Compliance Archive

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway to Screening System via gRPC/REST over mTLS
* Fraud Analyst and Risk Manager to Screening System via HTTPS and OAuth 2.0 / OIDC
* Screening System to Core Ledger / Compliance Archive via AWS S3 Object Lock / QLDB

## Technology Stack
* AWS Fargate / ECS: Chosen for container orchestration to reduce operational overhead for a 3-engineer team
* Go / Rust: Selected for stateless microservices to ensure sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS
* AWS S3 Object Lock / QLDB: Implemented for immutable, tamper-evident 7-year audit retention
* AWS KMS: Utilized for tokenization and cardholder data encryption at rest

## Rationale
[This architecture uses serverless containers and managed AWS services to minimize infrastructure complexity, fitting the €25k monthly budget and 3-engineer operational limit. Strict adherence to mTLS, tokenization, and WORM storage satisfies PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year auditability constraints.]

## Overview
[The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system processes card-not-present payment authorizations for a mid-size payment processor to detect fraud before approval, while providing case management for suspicious transactions.]
[It is built on AWS in eu-west-1, ensuring PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS, and tamper-evident auditability.]

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analyst & Risk Manager (Users)
* Payment Gateway / Acquirer, Payment Network / Card Brands, Core Ledger (External Systems)
* AWS API Gateway (Ingress/TLS Termination)
* Go Scoring Engine Container on AWS ECS on Fargate
* Node.js Case Management Container on AWS ECS on Fargate
* Amazon SQS / EventBridge (Asynchronous Audit Stream)
* Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 (Case State Database)
* AWS QLDB (Quantum Ledger Database)
* AWS Cognito & AWS Secrets Manager

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway to AWS API Gateway via HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
* API Gateway to Go Scoring Engine via gRPC over mTLS
* Go Scoring Engine to Amazon SQS / EventBridge via AWS SDK
* SQS to AWS QLDB for tamper-evident audit logging
* Node.js Case Management to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL via TLS
* Fraud Analysts to Node.js Case Management via HTTPS (OAuth2/OIDC via AWS Cognito)

## Technology Stack
* AWS ECS on Fargate: Container orchestration to eliminate OS patching for a 3-person team
* Go (Golang): High-performance language for the real-time scoring engine to meet sub-50ms P99 latency
* Node.js (TypeScript): Rapid development framework for the case management API
* Amazon QLDB: Cryptographic ledger ensuring tamper-evident 7-year audit retention
* AWS Signer & ECS Blue/Green: Secure immutable container deployment for risk-free model updates

## Rationale
[This serverless and containerized AWS architecture meets strict PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year audit requirements using managed security services like AWS QLDB and Cognito.]
[It satisfies high-throughput, low-latency performance (3,000 TPS under 50ms) using Go on Fargate while remaining operable by a 3-person team within a €25,000 monthly budget.]

AWS API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud prior to approval and provides a case management interface for fraud analysts. It is operated by a three-engineer team on AWS within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer (External System)
- AWS API Gateway (Ingress/TLS Termination Container)
- Go Scoring Engine (ECS Fargate Container)
- Node.js Case Management (ECS Fargate Container)
- Edge Router & WAF Integrator (API Gateway Component)
- Request Validator & Sanitizer (API Gateway Component)
- Upstream Router (API Gateway Component)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer -> AWS API Gateway: Sends payment authorizations via HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
- AWS API Gateway -> Go Scoring Engine: Routes scoring requests via gRPC over mTLS using AWS VPC Links and Network Load Balancers
- AWS API Gateway -> Node.js Case Management: Routes analyst review traffic via HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- AWS API Gateway: Chosen for native edge routing, WAF integration, and low latency without cold starts
- AWS WAF: Provides rate-limiting to protect the strict <50ms P99 latency SLA against DDoS
- AWS Secrets Manager: Stores mTLS client certificates securely for internal container routing
- Terraform / AWS CDK: Used for GitOps-based infrastructure deployment to comply with audit requirements

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless edge routing and managed container services to meet stringent <50ms P99 latency and PCI-DSS Level 1 security requirements. Lean managed AWS services keep operational overhead minimal for a three-engineer team within a strict budget.

Go Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
- High-performance Go scoring engine for real-time payment fraud screening.
- Processes payment authorizations to return approve, decline, or review decisions under strict latency constraints.

## Key Elements
- HTTP/gRPC Ingress Handler
- Feature Extractor Component
- Scoring & Evaluation Core
- Rule Engine Hot-Reloader Component
- Audit Signer Component
- Memory Sanitizer Middleware

## Relationships
- AWS API Gateway & NLB -> HTTP/gRPC Ingress Handler [gRPC over mTLS]
- Feature Extractor Component -> Amazon ElastiCache (Redis OSS) [TCP]
- Audit Signer Component -> AWS KMS [AWS SDK]
- Go Scoring Engine -> Amazon SQS / EventBridge [AWS SDK]

## Technology Stack
- Go (Golang): Chosen for low latency and high concurrency to meet <50ms P99 at 3,000 RPS.
- AWS ECS on Fargate: Chosen to maintain persistent cryptographic signing contexts.
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis OSS): Shared feature state caching to prevent DB drift.
- AWS KMS: Cryptographic signing for 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

## Rationale
- This architecture guarantees sub-50ms decision latencies while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 1-minute fail-open availability SLA.
- It operates within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget and can be managed by a three-engineer team.

Node.js Case Management.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and manages case reviews for analysts. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while maintaining strict auditability and high availability.

## Key Elements
- Node.js Case Management Container (Node.js/TypeScript on AWS ECS Fargate)
- API Router / Controller (Express/Fastify)
- Case Workflow Service
- Audit & Compliance Logger
- Data Access Repository (Prisma/TypeORM)
- Decision Feedback Publisher
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2
- AWS QLDB
- Amazon SQS / EventBridge
- AWS Cognito & AWS Secrets Manager
- AWS KMS

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst -> Node.js Case Management: Manages cases via HTTPS (OAuth2/OIDC via AWS Cognito)
- API Router -> Case Workflow Service: In-process function calls
- Case Workflow Service -> Data Access Repository: In-process calls
- Case Workflow Service -> Audit & Compliance Logger: Asynchronous event emission
- Audit & Compliance Logger -> AWS QLDB: Dispatches tamper-evident audit records via HTTPS/TLS (AWS SDK)
- Data Access Repository -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2: Reads/writes state via TLS with parameterization
- Case Workflow Service -> Decision Feedback Publisher: In-process event dispatch upon resolution
- Decision Feedback Publisher -> Amazon SQS / EventBridge: Publishes feedback messages via HTTPS/SigV4

## Technology Stack
- Node.js & TypeScript: Rapid development framework for case management APIs within engineering constraints.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration avoiding server management for a 3-engineer team.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2: Auto-scaling relational database fitting variable workloads within the budget.
- AWS QLDB: Tamper-evident ledger ensuring immutable, cryptographically verifiable 7-year audit trails.
- Amazon SQS / EventBridge: Decoupled asynchronous messaging for non-blocking feedback loops.
- AWS KMS: Field-level encryption and tokenization for PCI-DSS compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team while respecting a fixed budget. Strict boundary isolation, KMS encryption, and QLDB immutability satisfy rigorous PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability constraints.

Amazon SQS / EventBridge.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud before approval and provides case management for suspicious payments. It ensures sub-50ms latency, PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget operated by three engineers.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst & Risk Manager
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer
- Payment Network / Card Brands (Visa/Mastercard)
- Core Ledger / Compliance Archive
- AWS API Gateway (Ingress/TLS Termination)
- Go Scoring Engine (Go, AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Node.js Case Management (Node.js, AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Amazon EventBridge Bus (`fraud-events-bus`)
- Amazon SQS Queue (`audit-queue`) with Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ)
- Audit Buffer Worker (AWS Lambda)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2
- AWS QLDB
- AWS Cognito & AWS Secrets Manager

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst & Risk Manager -> AWS API Gateway: HTTPS over TLS 1.3 [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
- Payment Gateway -> AWS API Gateway: Payment authorization requests [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
- AWS API Gateway -> Go Scoring Engine: Routes authorization requests [HTTP/REST over AWS VPC PrivateLink]
- AWS API Gateway -> Node.js Case Management: Case review operations [HTTP/REST over AWS VPC PrivateLink]
- Go Scoring Engine -> Amazon EventBridge / SQS: Publishes scoring decisions and audit streams using batching [AWS SDK over AWS PrivateLink]
- Amazon SQS Queue -> Audit Buffer Worker: Long polling integration [AWS SDK]
- Audit Buffer Worker -> AWS QLDB: Writes tamper-evident audit logs [AWS QLDB Ledger API via AWS PrivateLink]
- Node.js Case Management -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2: Persists case data [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over AWS VPC PrivateLink]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS on Fargate: Runs containerized Go and Node.js workloads without server management for a 3-engineer team.
- Amazon EventBridge & SQS: Decouples real-time scoring from async auditing to maintain sub-50ms latency (R-04) and handle 3,000 TPS spikes.
- AWS Lambda: Buffer worker for cost-effective, auto-scaling QLDB ingestion within budget.
- AWS QLDB: Provides immutable, tamper-evident audit trails for 7-year compliance (R-06).
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2: Scalable relational storage for case management data.
- AWS KMS & PrivateLink: Enforces encryption-at-rest with segregated keys and isolates traffic from the public internet for PCI-DSS compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture uses fully managed AWS services to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team while staying under the 25,000 EUR budget. Asynchronous decoupling via SQS, EventBridge, and Lambda ensures the system meets the strict sub-50ms latency requirement (R-04) while guaranteeing 7-year auditability (R-06) and PCI-DSS compliance.

## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for a mid-size payment processor and manages fraud reviews. It ensures high-throughput, low-latency decisioning while meeting PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 7-year auditability mandate.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst & Risk Manager
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer, Payment Network / Card Brands (Visa/Mastercard), Core Ledger / Compliance Archive
- AWS API Gateway (Ingress/TLS Termination)
- Go Scoring Engine (Go (Golang), AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Node.js Case Management (Node.js (TypeScript), AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Amazon SQS / EventBridge
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 (Case state database)
- AWS QLDB
- AWS Cognito & AWS Secrets Manager

## Relationships
- AWS API Gateway -> Go Scoring Engine: Forwards authorization requests [HTTPS/REST]
- Go Scoring Engine -> Amazon SQS / EventBridge: Publishes suspicious transaction events [AMQP/EventBridge Protocol]
- Amazon SQS / EventBridge -> Node.js Case Management: Triggers case creation for analyst review [SQS Polling / Event Delivery]
- Node.js Case Management -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2: Reads and writes case state [PostgreSQL wire protocol over TLS 1.3 with IAM Auth]
- Node.js Case Management -> AWS QLDB: Stores immutable long-term audit logs [AWS SDK / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS (eu-west-1): Target cloud provider ensuring managed scalability and compliance tooling.
- Go (Golang) on AWS ECS on Fargate: High-performance runtime for sub-50ms P99 scoring latency.
- Node.js (TypeScript) on AWS ECS on Fargate: Efficient case management backend for analyst workflows.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2: Scalable relational storage with RLS for case state within cost constraints.
- AWS QLDB: Tamper-evident ledger ensuring tamper-resistant 7-year auditability (R-06).

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless containers and auto-scaling databases to handle 3,000 TPS within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It strictly isolates sensitive card data via encryption and IAM policies to guarantee PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 7-year audit trail for a 3-engineer team.

AWS QLDB.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations and provides case management for fraud analysts.]

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst & Risk Manager (Users)
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer, Payment Network / Card Brands (External Systems)
- AWS API Gateway (Ingress/TLS Termination)
- Go Scoring Engine (AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Node.js Case Management (AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Amazon SQS / EventBridge
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2
- AWS QLDB (Amazon QLDB) with Ledger Core, Audit Ingestion Service (AWS Lambda), and Verification & Export Worker (AWS Lambda)
- AWS Cognito & AWS Secrets Manager

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway -> AWS API Gateway: Submits payment authorization requests [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- Go Scoring Engine -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2: Reads/writes fraud rules and scoring data [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol / TLS]
- Go Scoring Engine -> Amazon SQS / EventBridge: Publishes scoring decisions and audit payloads [AWS SDK / HTTPS]
- Amazon SQS / EventBridge -> Audit Ingestion Service (AWS Lambda): Consumes audit payloads asynchronously [AWS SDK / SQS Polling]
- Audit Ingestion Service (AWS Lambda) -> AWS QLDB: Writes tamper-evident audit logs using PartQL [AWS SDK / HTTPS]
- Verification & Export Worker (AWS Lambda) -> AWS QLDB: Executes cryptographic digest verifications [AWS SDK / HTTPS]
- Verification & Export Worker (AWS Lambda) -> Amazon S3: Exports periodic cryptographic proofs [AWS SDK / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS on Fargate: Runs containerized Go and Node.js microservices without cluster management overhead.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2: Provides auto-scaling relational storage for rules and case management within budget.
- AWS QLDB: Delivers native cryptographic immutability and tamper-evident audit trails for PCI-DSS compliance.
- AWS Lambda (Python): Implements asynchronous audit ingestion and verification workers to minimize operational burden.
- AWS KMS: Secures ledger data at rest using Customer Managed Keys (CMK) with automated annual rotation.

## Rationale
- The architecture meets the sub-50ms P99 latency and high-throughput requirements by decoupling real-time scoring from asynchronous audit logging via Amazon SQS. It satisfies strict 7-year PCI-DSS compliance and auditability mandates using native AWS QLDB cryptographic verification without custom application overhead.

AWS Cognito & AWS Secrets Manager.analysis:
## Overview
The system provides real-time card-not-present payment fraud screening and case management for a mid-size payment processor. It evaluates authorization requests and supports analyst reviews under strict compliance and budget constraints.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst & Risk Manager
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer
- AWS API Gateway (Ingress/TLS Termination)
- Go Scoring Engine (AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Node.js Case Management (AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Amazon SQS / EventBridge
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2
- AWS QLDB
- AWS Cognito User Pool & Identity Pool
- Secrets Vault (AWS Secrets Manager)

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst -> AWS Cognito: HTTPS (TLS 1.3) via AWS API Gateway for OIDC/SAML authentication and federation
- Go Scoring Engine & Node.js Case Management -> AWS Secrets Manager: HTTPS over AWS PrivateLink (VPC Endpoints) using AWS SDK with IAM Task Roles
- Secrets Manager -> AWS KMS: HTTPS for encrypted storage using Customer Managed Keys (CMKs)
- API Gateway -> Go Scoring Engine & Node.js Case Management: HTTP/gRPC for secure internal routing

## Technology Stack
- AWS Cognito: Manages user authentication, federation, MFA, and 15-minute JWT generation without custom blocklist infrastructure
- AWS Secrets Manager: Secures database credentials and keys with Terraform-managed rotation and in-memory SDK caching for low latency
- Terraform: Manages infrastructure-as-code to prevent configuration drift and operational toil
- AWS CloudWatch: Monitors system health, logs, and canary synthetic transactions

## Rationale
This architecture uses native, fully managed AWS services to minimize operational toil for a three-engineer team while satisfying PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance. It maintains low latency, strict auditability, and robust security within a fixed 25,000 EUR monthly budget.
